causes.label: A potential problem has been detected with your machine.
remedies: Use the SmartHQ App to identify and troubleshoot the potential problem.
If you are not connected to WiFi, check your display for any codes and call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "A potential problem has been detected with your machine."

causes.label: There is a notification available in the SmartHQ App.
remedies: Use the SmartHQ App to follow recommended steps.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "There is a notification available in the SmartHQ App."

causes.label: The door was opened or the cycle was interrupted.
remedies: Press the Start pad once and close the door within 4 seconds to start the dishwasher.
Press the Start pad a second time when the dishwasher is running only if you wish to cancel the cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "The door was opened or the cycle was interrupted."

causes.label: This is a reminder that your dishwasher door has been left open during operation. It will continue beeping until you press Start and close the door.
remedies: Press Start and close the door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "This is a reminder that your dishwasher door has been left open during operation. It will continue beeping until you press Start and close the door."

symptoms.symptom: Beeping at the end of the cycle (on some models)

causes.label: This is normal. Dishwasher will beep twice at the end of the cycle.
remedies: To turn off the double beep indicator (or re-activate it if it was previously turned off), press the Dry Boost pad 5 times within 3 seconds.
A triple beep will sound to indicate the end-of-cycle beep option has been turned on or off.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "This is normal. Dishwasher will beep twice at the end of the cycle."

causes.label: Ultra-Fine Filter or Fine Filter is clogged
remedies: See the Care and Cleaning section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Ultra-Fine Filter or Fine Filter is clogged"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see the USING THE DISHWASHER section).
Turn on the hot water faucet nearest the dishwasher, let run until the water temperature stops rising.
Then start the dishwasher and turn off the faucet.
This ensures the entering water is hot.
Select Boost if available.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Water pressure is temporarily low
remedies: Turn on a faucet.
Is water coming out more slowly than usual?
If so, wait until pressure is normal before using your dishwasher.
Normal water pressure to the dishwasher should be 20-120 psi.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water pressure is temporarily low"

causes.label: Air gap or disposer clogged
remedies: Clean the air gap or flush the disposer.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Air gap or disposer clogged"

causes.label: High drain loop or air gap not installed
remedies: Refer to the Installation Instructions for proper drain line installation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "High drain loop or air gap not installed"

causes.label: Improper rack loading
remedies: Make sure large dishware does not block the detergent dispenser or the wash arms.
See the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Improper rack loading"

causes.label: Poor performing detergent
remedies: Use high quality detergents such as Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Bodewell Dishwasher Detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Poor performing detergent"

symptoms.symptom: Spots and filming on glasses and flatware

causes.label: Extremely hard water
remedies: Use high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid to prevent spots and prevent new film build-up.
If water is extremely hard, a softener may be required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Extremely hard water"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure water temperature is at least 120°F (49°C).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Overloading or improper loading of the dishwasher
remedies: Load dishwasher as shown in the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Overloading or improper loading of the dishwasher"

causes.label: Old or damp powder detergent

causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Old or damp powder detergent"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser empty
remedies: Refill with high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Rinse agent dispenser empty"

causes.label: Too little or low performing detergent
remedies: Make sure you use the proper amount of highly rated detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Too little or low performing detergent"

causes.label: Combination of soft water and too much detergent
remedies: This is called etching and is permanent.
To prevent this from happening, use less detergent if you have soft water.
Wash glassware in the shortest cycle that will get it clean.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Combination of soft water and too much detergent"

causes.label: Low performing phosphatefree detergent
remedies: See A white film on glassware, dishware and the interior in this TROUBLESHOOTING section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Low performing phosphatefree detergent"

causes.label: Water temperature entering the dishwasher exceeds 150°F
remedies: This could be etching.
Lower the water heater temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Water temperature entering the dishwasher exceeds 150°F"

symptoms.symptom: Slight odor coming from unit during dry portion of cycle

causes.label: This is normal when the Dry Boost option is used for the first time. It is caused by the heating of new parts and will disappear in a short time.
remedies: No action is required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "This is normal when the Dry Boost option is used for the first time. It is caused by the heating of new parts and will disappear in a short time."

causes.label: Wrong detergent
remedies: Use only high quality automatic dishwasher detergents to avoid sudsing.
Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Bodewell Dishwasher Detergent have been approved for use in all GE Appliances dishwashers.
To remove suds from the tub, open the dishwasher and let suds dissipate.
Open the door, press and hold Start for 3 seconds, and close the door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Wrong detergent"

causes.label: Rinse agent was spilled
remedies: Always wipe up rinse agent spills immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Rinse agent was spilled"

causes.label: Dishes or utensils are blocking the detergent cup
remedies: Reposition the dishes, so the water from the lower spray arm can flush the detergent cup.
See the Loading section.
Reposition the tall utensils or heavy silverware that may be keeping the dispenser cup door from opening.
See the Loading section.
Don’t place large bowls or pots directly under the detergent dispenser.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Dishes or utensils are blocking the detergent cup"

symptoms.symptom: Black or gray marks on dishes

remedies: Remove marks with a mild, abrasive cleaner.

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is at least 120°F.
Select Boost Dry.

symptoms.symptom: A white film on glassware, dishware and the interior

causes.label: This problem is likely caused by a low quality phosphatefree dishwasher detergent
remedies: To remove the white film, run your dishes through a dishwasher cycle with citric acid.
Use a WD35X151 citric acid kit found online.
Otherwise, use high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Dishwasher Cleaner or Finish® Dishwasher Cleaner found at your local grocery store.
Pour the citric acid in the detergent cup and close the cover.
Place the filmed but otherwise clean glassware and dishware in the dishwasher.
Leave silverware and other metal items out of the dishwasher.
Turn the dishwasher on and let it run through a complete cycle without detergent.
The glassware, dishware, and dishwasher should come out film free.
Alternatively, a vinegar rinse may be used.
Pour 1 cup of vinegar into dishwasher just after the detergent cup opens and let the dishwasher complete its cycle.
This may be repeated several times a year as needed.
The use of high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid may help minimize a repeat build up of film.
Also, the use of high quality detergents such as Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Bodewell Dishwasher Detergent will help prevent film build-up.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 24: "This problem is likely caused by a low quality phosphatefree dishwasher detergent"

remedies: Do not interrupt the cycle.
